messages:
Maya R: heads up — noticed a handful of customers hitting increased 429s after we started the rate-limit policy rollout at ~15:10 UTC. seeing both short bursts and steady retry loops. filing here so we can coordinate a quick mitigation.
Samir: which policy did we push? is this the new sliding-window limits (rate_limit_v2) or a token-bucket tweak?
Maya R: rate_limit_v2 canary enabled for 10% of tenants in prod-us-east. traffic pattern that tripped it looks like sudden multi-request spikes from some streaming ingestion jobs (lots of short-lived connections).
Liam: confirming, I see a spike in 429s correlating with canary tag: canary:v2-a at 15:12:02. quick query: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE status=429 AND canary='v2-a' GROUP BY tenant_id LIMIT 10;` — a couple of tenants are doing 300 req/min bursts.
Maya R: repro steps from support ticket: customer says their worker retries on 429s, causing retry storms. quoting them: "we bump into 429s, our lib retries every 200ms x 30 and then we get throttled for 1m."
OpsBot: deploy-event: rate_limit_v2 canary rollout 2026-01-21T15:09:54Z -> canary:v2-a (10%).
Noah: early thought: our new per-tenant sliding window is too aggressive for bursty clients. We intended to favor short bursts but maybe the smoothing window is too small causing immediate long penalties.
Samir: can we quickly flip canary off or reduce exposure? what's the safe command to revert?
Liam: we can pause the rollout via infra: `redwoodctl rollout pause --name rate_limit_v2` — that stops further propagation but leaves current canary nodes running. for immediate rollback: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --name rate_limit_v2 --to-tag canary:baseline` (this will start a canary rollback).
Maya R: prefer to put a short-term per-tenant override so impacted customers don't see more throttling while we diagnose. Is that possible without full rollback?
Noah: yes, we have tenant overrides. sample command: `redwoodctl config set tenant-override --tenant <TENANT_ID> --policy rate_limit_v1` — apply v1 behavior for that tenant only.
Emma: I can apply overrides for the top 3 affected tenants. need the tenant_ids from the log query.
Liam: attaching quick snippet I used to find tenants: ```
# find top 5 tenants with 429s in last 10m
select tenant_id, count(*) as errs from request_logs where status=429 and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' group by tenant_id order by errs desc limit 5;
```
Samir: while Emma applies overrides, let's also add a short-term change to limit penalty duration: reduce backoff window from 60s -> 15s for canary nodes. Noah, can you push a config change to the canary fleet?
Noah: yes, we can change `penalty_window_ms` on the canary config. updating now via infra API: `PATCH /internal/canary/config rate_limit_v2 {"penalty_window_ms":15000}`. will roll to canary nodes in ~30s.
Maya R: FYI support ticket says they also saw billing anomalies — their usage dropped and invoices flagged usage gaps. could be client retry loop + 429s. Billing team notified.
BillingBot: billing-alert: detected abrupt usage drop for tenant 12345 between 15:11-15:14 UTC. Suggest SMEs review before auto-invoice adjustments.
Emma: overrides applied for tenants 12345, 67890, 24680 — they confirm fewer 429s after ~15:22.
Liam: logs show 429 rate for those tenants dropped from 72% -> 8% after override. good.
Samir: plan: (1) pause further canary expansion, (2) apply per-tenant overrides for affected, (3) push penalty_window_ms -> 15000 on canary to reduce long penalties, (4) gather p95 latency/429s over next 30m, (5) decide rollback vs modify. agree?
Noah: agree. pausing expansion now. `redwoodctl rollout pause --name rate_limit_v2` returned success.
Maya R: support note: I've asked customers to disable aggressive retries for now (exponential backoff with jitter) and to share request traces. one customer dropped a trace showing many duplicate identical requests in <2s windows.
Liam: also noticed an edge where our rate-limiter counts multiple simultaneous connections separately; for streaming clients that open many short connections this double-counts. will add a ticket to infra to consider connection affinity in the limiter.
Samir: do we want to revert config change if things look worse after penalty change? keep rollback command ready.
Noah: rollback command is staged. I'll be on standby for a full rollback if p95 429s don't drop under 5% for canary by 16:00 UTC.
Maya R: support -> customers updated. one asked for ETA on full rollback, I gave ~45–60m pending telemetry.
BillingBot: billing-note: created ticket B-2026-009 to hold automated invoice adjustments for impacted tenants until manual review.
Emma: quick ask — is there a safe way to expose RateLimit headers to customers so they can smooth retries? they'd like details like `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.
Liam: we already return `Retry-After` on hard throttles, but for sliding-window soft-throttles we emit `X-RateLimit-Policy: rate_limit_v2` and `X-RateLimit-Reset: <unix-ts>`. we can add more granular remaining-count in a follow-up.
Maya R: summary for incident channel: will post a short TTL update once we see telemetry stabilized. thanks team — Emma, Liam, Noah, Samir, ops-bot.
OpsBot: incident-log: incident 2026-01-21-rlv2-canary created by Maya R at 15:17:03 UTC. state=investigating.
Noah: quick follow-up — we found two client libraries that aggressively retried on 429 without jitter. I opened PR requests to docs to recommend exponential backoff and included sample code.
Samir: once stable we should change rollout strategy: instead of 10% random tenants, pick low-risk tenants with known traffic patterns, and run a 1-hour traffic replay test against canary to exercise burst scenarios. added to postmortem TODOs.
Maya R: last update: at 15:47 — p95 429s for canary dropped to 3.2% after overrides + penalty tweak. I'm setting this thread to monitoring; will escalate if numbers climb again. thanks all.
Emma: closing tenant override tickets and leaving notes in customer profiles.
Liam: logging a follow-up infra ticket: RLIM-513: consider connection-affinity counting and improve headers for customers.
Samir: nice work. closing loop here. :thumbsup:
